| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.6.1** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 14.5.1] Verify that the application only responds to HTTP methods in use by the application or by the API (including OPTIONS during preflight requests) and unused methods (e.g., TRACE) are blocked. | 1 | 749 |

Problems to solve:

  * "the application only responds" - it is important to not execute funtionality if the used HTTP method is not meant for that action
  * TRACE is bit separate topic and I think we should have it covered somewhere in "V14 Configuration > V14.3 Unintended Information Leakage"

comments.body:
@elarlang what do you think about the following:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **13.6.1** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 14.5.1] Verify that only HTTP methods that are explicitly supported by the application or its API (including OPTIONS during preflight requests) can be used and that unused methods are blocked. | 1 | 749 |
| **14.3.7** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 14.5.1] Verify that the application does not leak data such as HTTP headers in response to the HTTP TRACE method. | 1 | 749 |
| **14.5.1** | [SPLIT TO 13.6.1, 14.3.7] | | |

14.3.7, attempt with a positive requirement:
> Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled to avoid potential information leakage.

Thanks, how about:

"_Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled or configured not to leak data such as HTTP headers._"

> ... not to leak data such as HTTP headers

This is a bit vague and "attackable". If we can be precise here - the leakage means only for those HTTP request header fields, that are added by intermediary layer, such as proxy or WAF, and are reflected back in the HTTP response body.

But this is describing how HTTP TRACE methods work. Personally, I think my last proposal is enough.
I think the merged version at the top is better. I don't think we need a split.
There are 2 different problems combined, it requires split.
